known_limitations: All results are local simulation (SIMULATOR_IDEAL/NOISY) or analytic under hypothetical parameters (SYNTHETIC). No calibration against any physical backend was available; noise parameters are hypothetical scenarios.
A simulator statevector is classical data copyable by the host; nothing here demonstrates software-level no-cloning.

Noise location model: one channel per note qubit between preparation and verification, plus readout error; gate-level noise on H/X is not modelled separately. Only single-channel NoiseSpec (no composition).

MVW 'optimal' label applies only to the W1 game per qubit (exact rational check = 3/4); it says nothing about W1_CV, W2 or noisy settings. The 8x8 unitary completion is synthesised generically (~18 CX) and is not a resource-optimal circuit.
Cloner circuits limited to n<=2 note qubits (3n<=8); larger n uses p^n, valid only for the independent per-qubit attack (MVW shows per-qubit is optimal for W1, not re-derived here).

Photonic model is phenomenological (independent photon loss, threshold detectors, independent dark counts, random-bit squashing for double clicks, single-mode thermal SPDC). No afterpulsing, dead time, timing jitter, detector efficiency mismatch or multimode SPDC. Not compared to measured photon statistics yet (needs lane E calibration).
Exact-match Wiesner verification collapses under realistic loss (photonic n=8 accept < 1e-6 at 3 dB, mu=0.1); a loss/threshold-tolerant verifier is game W2 and has no closed form assumed here.
MeasurementEvent times use a logical simulator clock (event_time_utc_ns = start + shot index, accuracy 0) and are not UTC; each shot is a freshly prepared note.
Figure 10 plot not rendered; data is in handoffs/F-F1_evidence.json (honest_acceptance_curves, aer_noisy_points, verify_circuit_resources).
